props.gloss_en: the slaughter of a Kuti is permitted -- when a Jew stands over him
but if the Jew came and found that he had slaughtered, he cuts an olive-bulk and gives it to him: if he ate it, it is permitted to eat of his slaughter; if not, forbidden
likewise, if he found in his hand a string of birds, he severs the head of one of them and gives it to him: if he ate it, permitted; if not, forbidden
Abaye, from the first clause: only when a Jew stands over him; if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is not permitted
Rava, from the last clause: only where he came and found it already slaughtered is the test needed; if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is fine
Rav Menashe: the case is where the Jew tucks the birds under his wing, so the Kuti cannot know which he will be given
Rav Mesharshiya: the Jew mangles the birds' necks, so any mark the Kuti left is effaced
are the five disqualifications of slaughter written in the Torah? rather, once the Kutim embraced them, they embraced them; here too, once they embraced bird slaughter, they embraced it
whether Kutim are relied on for an unwritten mitzva they embraced is a tannaitic dispute
the matza of a Kuti is permitted, and a person fulfils his obligation with it on Pesach
R' Elazar forbids it, since they are not expert in the fine points of mitzvot like Jews
RSBG: every mitzva the Kutim embraced, they are far more meticulous in than Jews
what the tanna kamma's clause teaches: the Kutim ARE expert in guarding matza from leavening
R' Elazar's ground: they are not expert in guarding matza
first proposal: the tanna kamma and RSBG differ over a written mitzva the Kutim did not embrace (tk: relied on since written; RSBG: only if embraced)
second proposal: they differ over an unwritten mitzva the Kutim did embrace
the tanna kamma: since it is unwritten, even if they embraced it they are not relied on
RSBG: once they embraced it, they embraced it, written or not
Rava: a Jewish apostate who eats carcasses for appetite -- one checks a knife and gives it to him, and it is permitted to eat of his slaughter
the reason: where both the permitted and the forbidden are available, he will not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden
the baraita: the chametz of transgressors after Pesach is permitted immediately, because they exchange it
R' Yehuda: chametz after Pesach is forbidden by Torah law
R' Shimon: chametz after Pesach is forbidden by rabbinic law
the baraita does not say 'for I say they exchanged' but 'because they exchange' -- they certainly exchange
the baraita: all may slaughter -- even a Kuti, even an uncircumcised man, even a Jewish apostate
eliminated: the arel is one whose brothers died of circumcision -- but he is a proper Jew, so need not be listed
rather, obviously the arel is an apostate with regard to circumcision
and the baraita holds: an apostate for one thing is not an apostate for the entire Torah
the apostate of the last clause is an apostate for that very thing (eating carcasses) -- like Rava
an apostate for that very thing may not slaughter: since he is habituated to it, it seems to him permitted
the apostate of the last clause is an apostate for idolatry -- like Rav Anan
idolatry is grave: whoever repudiates it is as one who acknowledges the entire Torah
Rav Anan in Shmuel's name: a Jewish apostate for idolatry -- it is permitted to eat of his slaughter

for we find that Jehoshaphat king of Judah benefited from Ahab's feast, as it says: 'and Ahab slaughtered sheep and oxen for him in abundance... and incited him to go up to Ramot Gilead' (II Chr 18:2)
incitement is not by words alone
Jehoshaphat would not set himself apart from Ahab [at table]
proposed source: 'I am as you, my people as your people' (I Kings 22:4) -- eliminated: then 'my horses as your horses' too?

rather from here: the two kings sat each on his throne 'in a threshing floor at the gate of Samaria' (I Kings 22:10) -- like a threshing floor, as the mishna says the Sanhedrin sat as half a round threshing floor: they sat together as one court
'and the ravens brought him bread and meat' (I Kings 17:6) -- Rav: from Ahab's butchers
Ravina: 'orvim' means actual ravens
R' Pedat: 'a little maiden' (II Kings 5:2) -- 'naara' names her place, Neoran
'of you' (Lev 1:2) -- not all of you: to exclude the apostate [from bringing offerings]
'of you' -- among you I distinguished, not among the nations
'of the animals' -- to include people who resemble animals
hence they said: offerings are accepted from Jewish transgressors, so that they may return in repentance
except the apostate, and one who pours wine to idols, and one who desecrates Shabbat in public
the first clause excludes an apostate for the entire Torah
the middle clause accepts from an apostate for one thing
eliminated: the seifa's apostate is an apostate for the whole Torah -- that is the first clause
eliminated: the seifa's apostate is an apostate for one thing -- the middle clause contradicts
rather it says: except one who is an apostate to pour wine to idols and to desecrate Shabbat in public
so an apostate for idolatry is an apostate for the entire Torah
'from the people of the land' (Lev 4:27) -- to exclude an apostate [from the sin offering]
R' Shimon: 'which may not be done, in error, and is guilty' -- one who would turn back on learning brings an offering for his error; one who would not, does not
Rav Hamnuna: they differ over an apostate for eating forbidden fat who brings an offering for [unwittingly eating] blood

one verse is for the sin offering (מעם הארץ) and one for the burnt offering (מכם), and both are needed: a sin offering atones, a burnt offering is a gift; a burnt offering is voluntary, a sin offering obligatory
'man and beast You save, Lord' (Ps 36:7) -- Rav: these are people shrewd in knowledge who make themselves like beasts
where 'man and beast' is written it is praise; 'beast' alone is pejorative
Rabban Gamliel and his court voted on the slaughter of a Kuti and forbade it
R' Zeira: perhaps the master heard the prohibition only where no Jew stands over him?
R' Assi: I saw R' Yochanan eat of a Kuti's slaughter
R' Assi too ate of a Kuti's slaughter
R' Zeira resolved it himself: it is reasonable that they heard the prohibition and did not accept it
R' Zeira accepted R' Yaakov bar Idi's rejection of his restriction
the old man to R' Shimon ben Elazar: 'put a knife to your throat if you are a man of appetite' (Prov 23:2)
R' Shimon ben Elazar reported it to R' Meir, and R' Meir decreed against them -- the answer to ומאי טעמא גזרו בהו רבנן
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: they found them with the image of a dove on top of Mount Gerizim, which they worshipped
R' Meir follows his own view: he takes account of a minority, and decreed against the majority on account of the minority
Rabban Gamliel and his court also hold like R' Meir

R' Chiyya: the verse's plain sense concerns a student before his teacher -- if the teacher can answer him, ask; if not, consider, and 'put a knife to your throat': if you are a man of spirit, separate from him
the old man to R' Yitzchak ben Yosef: there are no Torah-keepers here
R' Ami and R' Assi did not move from there until they made the Kutim complete gentiles
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'complete gentiles' means as to renouncing and transferring domain [for an eruv]
an apostate Jew who keeps Shabbat in the market renounces and transfers domain; one who does not, does not
because they said: a Jew transfers and renounces domain, but with a gentile only by renting
how? he says 'my domain is acquired by you' or 'is renounced to you' -- the other acquires, and need not perform an act of acquisition
at an inn they were served eggs cooked down in wine; R' Zeira did not eat
and Rav Assi ate
R' Zeira: is the master not concerned about a demai mixture? Rav Assi: it did not occur to me
R' Zeira: they did not decree on a demai mixture -- it is permitted (is it possible that Rav Assi would come to eat the forbidden?)
the mishna: one who buys wine to put into brine, or vetch for meal, or lentils for groats, is obligated for demai
but the [bought] products themselves are permitted, because they are a mixture
the baraita: one who gives his neighbour dough to bake or a pot to cook need not be concerned for her leaven and spices
but if he said 'make it for me from yours', he must be concerned for her leaven and spices, for shevi'it and for tithes
the premise the three challenges probe: one is not concerned that the other party exchanged [tithed for untithed]
the mishna: one who gives to his mother-in-law tithes what he gives her and what he takes from her, for she is suspected of exchanging what spoils
R' Yehuda: she wants her daughter's good and is ashamed before her son-in-law
the mishna: one who gives to his innkeeper tithes what he gives and what he takes back, for she is suspected of exchanging
the wife of a chaver may grind with the wife of an am haaretz when she [the chaver's wife] is impure, but not when pure
R' Shimon ben Elazar: even when impure she may not grind, because her companion gives her [grain] and she eats
R' Yehoshua ben Zeruz testified before Rebbi that R' Meir ate a vegetable leaf [untithed] in Beit She'an
and on his account Rebbi permitted [the produce of] all Beit She'an [without tithing]
Rebbi's derasha on II Kings 18:4: could Asa and Jehoshaphat, who destroyed all idolatry, have left the bronze serpent? -- they left it for Hezekiah to distinguish himself
his fathers left Hezekiah room to distinguish himself; so my fathers left me room to distinguish myself
hence a Torah scholar who states a halakha is not moved / dismissed / made arrogant (three wordings, each derived at 7a.3)
'and Menashe did not drive out Beit She'an and its towns' (Judg 1:27) -- so Beit She'an is of the Land
many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt and not by those who came up from Babylonia
and he holds: the first sanctification sanctified for its time and not for the future; and they left these cities [unsanctified] for the poor to rely on in the sabbatical year
R' Zeira: he ate it from a bundle -- and a bundled vegetable is obligated from when it is bundled
the mishna: a vegetable that is bundled [becomes liable to tithes] once it is bundled
R' Pinchas ben Yair, on his way to redeem captives: Ginai, part your waters for me and I will cross
Ginai: you go to do your Maker's will and I go to do mine; you may or may not accomplish it, I certainly do
R' Pinchas ben Yair: if you do not part, I decree that water never pass through you
the river parted for him, then for a man carrying wheat for Pesach (he is busy with a mitzva), then for an Arab merchant accompanying them (lest he say 'this is how they treat companions')
Rav Yosef: how much greater is this man than Moses and the 600,000 -- there once, here three times
rather, he is like Moses and the 600,000
R' Pinchas ben Yair (when his donkey refused the barley until it was tithed): this poor creature goes to do its Maker's will and you feed it untithed produce!
the mishna: one who buys for seed or for an animal, flour for hides, oil for a lamp or for greasing vessels, is exempt from demai
R' Yochanan: this was taught only where he bought them initially for the animal; if he bought them for people and changed his mind for the animal, he must tithe
the baraita: one who buys produce in the market to eat and changes his mind for an animal may not put it before his or another's animal unless he tithed
R' Pinchas ben Yair to Rebbi: do you think I am vowed from benefit from Jews? Israel are holy -- some want to host and have not, some have and want not; you want and you have
'do not eat the bread of the stingy... eat and drink he will say to you, but his heart is not with you' (Prov 23:6-7)
but now I am in a hurry, for I am occupied with a mitzva; when I return I will come in to you
seeing white mules at the entrance: the angel of death is in this man's house, and I should dine with him?
Rebbi: I will sell them -- R' Pinchas ben Yair: 'do not put a stumbling block before the blind' (Lev 19:14)
I will declare them ownerless -- you multiply the damage
I will hamstring them -- that is cruelty to animals
I will kill them -- that is wanton destruction
R' Chama bar Chanina: the righteous are greater in their death than in their life
as it says: the man thrown into Elisha's grave touched Elisha's bones and lived and stood on his feet (II Kings 13:21)
the baraita: he stood on his feet but did not go home [he did not truly live on]
R' Yochanan: Elijah's double portion was fulfilled when Elisha cured Naaman's leprosy, which equals death, as it says 'let her not be as one dead' (Num 12:12)
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: why are they [the mules] called yemim (Gen 36:24)? because their terror lies upon creatures
R' Chanina: in my days no one ever asked me about the kick of a white mule and lived
read rather: [no one asked me] and the wound healed
'there is none beside Him' (Deut 4:35) -- R' Chanina: not even sorcery
R' Chanina to the woman taking dust from under his feet: take it; your scheme will not succeed -- 'there is none beside Him' is written
R' Yochanan: why are they called keshafim? because they contradict the heavenly household
R' Chanina: no one bruises his finger below unless it is proclaimed above
as it says: 'a man's steps are from the Lord' (Prov 20:24)
R' Elazar: the blood of a bruise atones like the blood of a burnt offering
Rava: [that is] the right thumb, on a second bruising, and when he is going to a mitzva
R' Pinchas ben Yair never broke bread that was not his own, and from his maturity never benefited even from his father's table

answered_by.gloss_en: ולטעמיך, שהייה דרסה חלדה הגרמה ועיקור מי כתיבן? אלא כיון דאחזיקו -- אחזיקו (= p_kevan_deachzuku)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, כי לא בדק נמי -- if he will not leave the permitted, why must one check the knife at all?

answered_by.gloss_en: מיטרח לא טרח -- he will not trouble himself to check the knife

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא מיזבח זבח, מיכל לא אכל! -- perhaps Ahab slaughtered but Jehoshaphat did not eat

answered_by.gloss_en: ויסיתהו כתיב -- 'and he incited him': through the feast

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא בדברים -- perhaps he incited him with words

answered_by.gloss_en: אין הסתה בדברים (= p_ein_hasata_bidvarim)

objections.gloss_en: ולא? והכתיב כי יסיתך אחיך (Deut 13:7) -- the inciter to idolatry incites with words

answered_by.gloss_en: באכילה ובשתיה -- he too incites with food and drink

objections.gloss_en: והכתיב ותסיתני בו לבלעו חנם (Job 2:3) -- God was 'incited' by words

answered_by.gloss_en: למעלה שאני -- above it is different

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא משתא אשתי, מיכל לא אכל? -- perhaps he only drank. (The stam's attempted dismissal -- מאי שנא שתיה, an idolater is not an apostate for the whole Torah -- is itself rejected at 4b.12: הכי השתא? the wine was ordinary gentile wine, not yet forbidden; eating may differ.)

answered_by.gloss_en: איבעית אימא: לאו אורחיה דמלכא משתיא בלא מיכלא -- a king does not drink without eating
ואיבעית אימא: ויזבח ... ויסיתהו כתיב -- במה הסיתו? בזביחה -- the incitement was by the slaughtering

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא עובדיה זבח? -- perhaps the God-fearing Obadiah slaughtered

answered_by.gloss_en: לרוב כתיב, עובדיה לא הוה ספיק -- 'in abundance': Obadiah alone could not have managed

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא שבעת אלפים זבוח? (I Kings 19:18) -- perhaps the seven thousand who did not bow to Baal slaughtered

answered_by.gloss_en: טמורי הוו מיטמרי מאיזבל -- they were hiding from Jezebel

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא גברי דאחאב הוו מעלו? -- perhaps Ahab's men were proper

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב: מושל מקשיב על דבר שקר כל משרתיו רשעים (Prov 29:12)

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא גברי דיהושפט נמי לא הוו מעלו -- Ahab's men slaughtered and Jehoshaphat's men ate; Obadiah slaughtered and Jehoshaphat ate

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, מדמושל מקשיב על דבר שקר כל משרתיו רשעים -- הא לדבר אמת משרתיו צדיקים

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא זבוח גברי דאחאב אכל אחאב וגבריה, זבוח גברי דיהושפט אכל יהושפט וגבריה? -- perhaps each king ate his own men's slaughter

answered_by.gloss_en: לא הוה מפליג נפשיה מיניה (= p_lo_mafleig_nafshei; its source is the frame f_lo_mafleig_menalan)

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא תרי גברי דהוי שמייהו עורבים! מי לא כתיב: ויהרגו את עורב בצור עורב (Judg 7:25)?

answered_by.gloss_en: איתרמאי מילתא דתרוייהו הוה שמייהו עורבים? -- that both happened to be named Orev?

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא על שם מקומן! -- as R' Pedat read נערה קטנה by her place of origin

answered_by.gloss_en: אם כן עורביים מיבעי ליה -- then it would say 'Orevites'

objections.gloss_en: הא גופא קשיא: אמרת מכם ולא כולכם להוציא את המשומד, והדר תני מקבלין קרבנות מפושעי ישראל!

answered_by.gloss_en: הא לא קשיא: רישא -- משומד לכל התורה כולה, מציעתא -- משומד לדבר אחד (= p_reisha_mumar_lekol, p_metziata_mumar_ledavar_echad)

objections.gloss_en: וכל היכא דכתיב בהמה גריעותא היא? והכתיב אדם ובהמה תושיע ה', ואמר רב יהודה אמר רב: ... ערומין בדעת

answered_by.gloss_en: התם כתיב אדם ובהמה, הכא בהמה לחודיה כתיב (= p_adam_uvehema_meulyuta)

objections.gloss_en: וכל היכא דכתיב אדם ובהמה מעליותא היא? והא כתיב: וזרעתי את בית ישראל זרע אדם וזרע בהמה (Jer 31:26)

answered_by.gloss_en: התם הא חלקיה קרא -- זרע אדם לחוד וזרע בהמה לחוד

objections.gloss_en: דמי האי מרבנן כדלא גמירי אינשי שמעתא -- בשאין ישראל עומד על גביו למימרא בעי? -- that case needs no vote; R' Zeira accepted the rebuke (6a.1)
למאי? אי לשחיטה ויין נסך -- מהתם גזרו בהו רבנן! -- the decrees on their slaughter and wine were made generations earlier

answered_by.gloss_en: אינהו גזור ולא קבילו מינייהו, אתו רבי אמי ורבי אסי גזרו וקבילו מינייהו -- the earlier decree was not accepted; this one was

objections.gloss_en: ולא גזרו על תערובת דמאי? והתניא ... עשי לי משליכי -- חושש לשאור ותבלין שבה

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני התם, דכיון דקאמר לה עשי לי משליכי, כמאן דעריב בידים דמי -- there he mixed it as if by hand
שאני שאור ותבלין, דלטעמא עביד, וטעמא לא בטיל -- leaven and spices are for flavour, and flavour is not nullified

objections.gloss_en: ולחלופי לא חיישינן? והתנן: הנותן לחמותו ... מפני שחשודה מחלפת המתקלקל

answered_by.gloss_en: התם כדתניא טעמא -- R' Yehuda's reason (= p_ry_rotza_betakanat_bita): a special motive, not a general suspicion

objections.gloss_en: ולעלמא לא חיישינן? והתנן: הנותן לפונדקית שלו ... מפני שחשודה מחלפת

answered_by.gloss_en: התם נמי מוריא ואמרה: בר בי רב ליכול חמימא ואנא איכול קרירא -- she rationalizes: the scholar should eat hot food, I will eat cold

objections.gloss_en: ולחלופי לא חיישינן? והתניא: אשת חבר טוחנת ... ר' שמעון בן אלעזר: אף בזמן שהיא טמאה לא תטחון -- השתא מיגזל גזלה, חלופי מיבעיא?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם נמי מוריא ואמרה: תורא מדישיה קאכיל -- she rationalizes: the ox eats from its own threshing

objections.gloss_en: מקום שאבותיך ואבות אבותיך נהגו בו איסור, אתה תנהוג בו היתר?

answered_by.gloss_en: דרש להן ... אלא מקום הניחו לו אבותיו להתגדר בו, אף אני מקום הניחו לי אבותי (= p_makom_hinichu_li)

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה: ומי איכא למאן דאמר דבית שאן לאו מארץ ישראל היא? והכתיב ולא הוריש מנשה את בית שאן

answered_by.gloss_en: אישתמיטתיה הא דאמר ... הרבה כרכים כבשום עולי מצרים ולא כבשום עולי בבל (= p_harbe_krachim), וקסבר קדושה ראשונה קדשה לשעתה (= p_kedusha_rishona_lishata)

objections.gloss_en: והא רבי מאיר עלה בעלמא הוא דאכיל! -- a mere leaf, not yet liable to tithes, proves nothing about Beit She'an

answered_by.gloss_en: מאגודה אכליה, ותנן: ירק הנאגד משיאגד (= p_rm_achal_meaguda)

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא לאו אדעתיה? -- perhaps it did not occur to R' Meir (Steinsaltz: R' Yirmeya asks)

answered_by.gloss_en: השתא בהמתן של צדיקים ... צדיקים עצמן לא כל שכן (the kal vachomer kv_behemtan_tzaddikim_r_meir)

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא עישר עליהם ממקום אחר? -- perhaps he tithed for it from elsewhere

answered_by.gloss_en: לא נחשדו חברים לתרום שלא מן המוקף -- chaverim are not suspected of separating from non-adjacent produce

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא נתן עיניו בצד זה ואכל בצד אחר? -- perhaps he designated one side and ate from the other

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר ליה: חזי מאן גברא רבה קמסהיד עליה -- see what great man testifies about him

objections.gloss_en: ודלמא הכא נמי חדא זימנא? -- perhaps here too it was one parting; left standing, replaced by אלא כמשה (= p_kemoshe)
ומי מיחייבא? והתנן: הלוקח ... לבהמה ... פטור מהדמאי

answered_by.gloss_en: התם הא אתמר עלה -- R' Yochanan's limitation (= p_ry_lo_shanu_livhema): only if bought for an animal from the start

objections.gloss_en: ודילמא לקיומי ביה ברכתא דאליהו, דכתיב: ויהי נא פי שנים ברוחך אלי? -- perhaps the revival fulfilled Elijah's blessing of a double portion, and shows nothing about the dead

answered_by.gloss_en: אי הכי, היינו דתניא: על רגליו עמד ולביתו לא הלך? -- a revival that did not last cannot count for the blessing (= p_al_raglav_amad)

objections.gloss_en: והא קחזינא דחיי! -- we see such people live

answered_by.gloss_en: אימא: וחיית (= p_eima_vechayat)

objections.gloss_en: והא קחזינא דמיתסי! -- we see the wound heal

answered_by.gloss_en: דחיוורן ריש כרעייהו קא אמרינן -- we speak of those white at the top of their legs

objections.gloss_en: והאמר רבי יוחנן: למה נקרא שמן כשפים -- שמכחישין פמליא של מעלה! -- sorcery does work

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני רבי חנינא דנפישא זכותיה -- R' Chanina is different, his merit being great
